questions.text:
Refer to Text A, "Matariki".

How do the writer's language choices help us to understand their experience of Matariki? You might consider how they have used:
• references to time
• ideas about the activities during the celebration
• ideas about whanau and belonging.

Support your explanation with quotes and examples of language features from the text.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identify/describe aspects of the text relevant to the question, explain how one or more aspects create meaning. Merit: Explain how two or more aspects work together to create meaning. Excellence: Explain how aspects have been deliberately used to create meanings and effects relating to the writer's purpose and wider contexts. Ideas might include: varied syntax, sentences, and structure (e.g. repetition of 'Matariki' at beginning of first three paragraphs) conveys building excitement and anticipation of celebration stages; winter predawn cold and darkness is a special start to a new day (personification and listing); contrast of past with present ('Polynesian lore' minds and 'internet age' minds); traditions/beliefs connect people throughout time, belonging/togetherness rekindled every year by a tradition where people gather.

questions.text:
Refer to Text B, "the road and the rain".

How does the writer help us to understand the experience of the journey? You might consider how they have used:
• mood or atmosphere
• ideas about life as a journey
• observations of the environment
• ideas about past and present.

Support your explanation with quotes and examples of language features from the text.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identify/describe aspects of the text relevant to the question, explain how one or more aspects create meaning. Merit: Explain how two or more aspects work together to create meaning. Excellence: Explain how aspects have been deliberately used to create meanings and effects relating to the writer's purpose and wider contexts. Ideas might include: the road as a metaphor or symbol for life as a journey, leading to the past (ancestors' graveyard and home) and into the future; weather reflects the writer's gloomy or sombre mood; the bird as a metaphor or symbol for hope, or the struggle of the individual; the train as a metaphor or symbol for life, suggesting that moving forward can be slow/hard work when carrying the burden of the past.

questions.text:
Refer to Text C, "The Beach".

How does the writer help us to understand people's experiences of the beach? You might consider how they have used:
• ideas about what people do at the beach
• ideas about what people feel about the outdoors.

Support your explanation with quotes and examples of language features from the text.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identify/describe aspects of the text relevant to the question, explain how one or more aspects create meaning. Merit: Explain how two or more aspects work together to create meaning. Excellence: Explain how aspects have been deliberately used to create meanings and effects relating to the writer's purpose and wider contexts. Ideas might include: how we behave at the boundaries of our comfort zone, seeking to recreate a home-like environment (metaphor of 'open house') in the outdoors; the fun/excitement/liberation of feeling like we are exploring and conquering the land (rhetorical question: 'what do we do?'); how nature is something beyond our control (sentence variation), which motivates our curiosity.
